human_tolerance.notes: Breeding habitat is 'urban and suburban areas across North America'; about 40 million birds are estimated across North America (Partners in Flight); frequent year-round visitors to sunflower and nyjer feeders, where they congregate and are 'aggressive enough to drive other birds away'. flight_distance_m and light_max are judgement, not separately sourced numbers.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: The female lays clutches from February through August, two or more broods per year with 2 to 6 eggs per brood, most commonly 4 or 5, usually one egg per morning. Eggs are pale bluish-green with few black spots; incubation 12-14 days by the female alone; young fledge at about 11 to 19 days after hatching. Analyses of California nest records found egg-laying occurred significantly earlier in warmer springs.

phases.name: nesting
phases.note: The female builds the nest, sometimes in as little as two days, of twigs and debris forming a cup, usually 1.8-2.7 m above the ground in a cavity: an opening in a building, a hanging plant, another cup-shaped outdoor decoration, or a nest abandoned by another bird. Nests may be reused for later broods or in following years.

phases.name: territorial
phases.note: Males hold a breeding territory through courtship and nesting, feeding the female during courtship, breeding and incubation, and raising of the young; the male is the primary feeder of the fledglings.

phases.name: dispersal
phases.note: 'House finches are mainly permanent residents throughout their range; some birds migrate to the south, with adult females moving longer distances than males.' No migration window is given in the source, so the window is aligned to the post-breeding period.

vocalizations.description: 'The house finch's songs typically consist of a series of high-pitched musical jumbles ending with a distinct high note, wheer.' Sung from a perch or a feeder through the breeding season; the warbling song is commonly heard in residential streets.
'Calls from flight include a soft cheet or wheat, with perched birds giving a more drawn-out version.' It doubles as the alarm call, since the source describes no separate alarm vocalisation.

conservation.note: 'The house finch is assessed as "Least Concern" on the IUCN Red List due to its extensive range, increasing population trend, and large population size.'

range.note: 'It is native to Mexico and southwestern United States, but has since been introduced to the eastern part of North America and Hawai'i, and is found year-round in almost all parts of the United States and most of Mexico'. Only the states the source names are listed: southwestern states plus US-CO for the northern edge of the western range (the source does not resolve where Colorado's birds came from, and the species is resident and established across the state), and US-NY plus US-HI for the two documented introductions (the 1940s New York release and the 19th-century Hawaiian introduction). The eastern introduced population is described as covering 'the eastern U.S.' without itemising states, so no further states are listed. No elevation range is given in the source, so elevation_m is omitted.

traits.note: Covers the structural traits (body plan, limb count, thermoregulation, skin, flight, respiration, metamorphosis, perching) and locomotion modes: a small passerine that 'forage[s] on the ground or in vegetation normally' and flies between feeding sites and roosts. Individual numeric and behavioural traits below carry their own entries.

traits.nest_type.note: 'Nests are made in cavities, including openings in buildings, hanging plants, and other cup-shaped outdoor decorations. Sometimes nests abandoned by other birds are used.'

traits.size_class.note: From mass_kg (~0.021 kg, a 21 g average and a 16-27 g range); the validator's size-class bands place this at the bottom of the scale, in the Tiny band.

traits.mass_kg.note: 'Body mass can vary from 16 to 27 g, with an average weight of 21 g' - a directly stated figure.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Midpoint of the stated 20-25 cm wingspan, as a direct conversion of the sourced value.

traits.lifespan_y.note: HONEST GAP: no lifespan figure for Haemorhous mexicanus was found in any CC0 or CC BY source. Wikipedia's House finch article gives none, and the Animal Diversity Web account (CC BY-NC-SA, last resort) could not be retrieved. The value is therefore inferred from a close relative in the sense AGENTS.md allows: the American goldfinch (Spinus tristis), the finch this species' abundance is ranked behind, has a recorded oldest wild bird of 10 years 5 months (Wikipedia). Treating that maximum as about twice the typical wild lifespan of a small granivorous songbird gives 5.0 years. This is an order-of-magnitude figure, not a measured value for this species.

traits.diet.note: Feeding section: 'They primarily eat grains, seeds and berries, being voracious consumers of weed seeds such as nettle and dandelion; included are incidental small insects such as aphids.' Shares follow that ordering - seeds and grain together dominant, fruit and berries next, insects explicitly incidental. The schema has no separate grain key, so grain is folded into seed.

traits.social.note: The male feeds the female throughout courtship, breeding, incubation and rearing and is the primary feeder of the fledglings, which is a pair-centred breeding system; non-breeding birds congregate in numbers at feeders. The source does not state pair duration explicitly.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Judgement: a diurnal feeder and garden bird; the source gives daytime feeder visits and a flight call but does not label the pattern.

traits.defense.note: Judgement: 'House finches are aggressive enough to drive other birds away from places such as feeders', but the shared perching-songbird program responds to a close threat by moving away, so Flee was authored for the dominant escape response.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: among the tamest garden birds - it nests in building openings, visits feeders constantly and is 'found year-round in almost all parts of the United States' - so a low wariness value was authored.

habitat.note: Covers shelter_tag and habitat.resources. Seed, fruit, berry and invertebrate tags come from the Feeding section; cavity from the Breeding section; perch from perching in shrubs and at feeders. Weights are judgement, not separately sourced percentages.

habitat.use.note: Feeding and habitat statements: 'House finches forage on the ground or in vegetation normally', they perch at feeders and sing from perches, and they make short flights between feeding sites and roosts. Split between ground foraging, vegetation and flight is judgement; the source gives no numeric split.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: 'Their breeding habitat is urban and suburban areas across North America', 'They are frequent visitors to bird feeders throughout the year', about 40 million birds across North America (Partners in Flight), and nests in building openings and hanging plants. flight_distance_m and light_max are judgement, not separately sourced numbers.

seasonal.strategy.note: 'House finches are mainly permanent residents throughout their range; some birds migrate to the south, with adult females moving longer distances than males', and the species is 'found year-round in almost all parts of the United States'. ActiveYearRound was used rather than PartialMigration because the resident majority, not a winter fraction, is the species' defining pattern and the schema's winter_fraction would have to describe a minority.

seasonal.phases.note: Breeding February to August with two or more broods and the quoted clutch, incubation and fledging figures, nest construction by the female, year-round pair-centred territorial behaviour through the nesting period, and a light southern movement by part of the population. Day-of-month boundaries other than 'February through August' are judgement; the source gives no migration window, so the dispersal window is aligned to the post-breeding period and labelled. The breeding phase is tagged US-CO because the locale that prompted this record is in Colorado; the source's dates are continental.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Egg (pale bluish-green with few black spots), altricial juvenile (hatchlings pink with closed eyes and down, silent for the first seven or eight days then peeping during feedings, fledging at 11-19 days) and adult. Notable for this record: house finches are 'one of the few birds who feed their young only plant matter'. No sourced juvenile-plumage duration was found, so duration_days is unset and the juvenile scale is judgement.

vocalizations.song.note: Description section: 'The house finch's songs typically consist of a series of high-pitched musical jumbles ending with a distinct high note, wheer.' season_months is aligned to the February-August breeding season because the source dates song only implicitly.

look.note: Description section: 'Adults have a long, square-tipped brown tail and are a brown or dull-brown color across the back with some shading into deep gray on the wing feathers. Breast and belly feathers may be streaked... In most cases, adult males' heads, necks and shoulders are reddish', the colour 'derived from the berries and fruits in its diet', ranging 'from pale straw-yellow through bright orange to deep, intense red'; 'Adult females have brown upperparts and streaked underparts'. The palette puts the male's red on the head and a streaked tan underpart wash on the belly; proportions are authored judgement.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program: food_tag is seed, the largest diet share, which the program uses for foraging at feeders and on the ground; flee_m and wariness reflect a bird that tolerates people closely; nest_m1/nest_m2 span the February-August breeding season.

vocalizations.flight_call.note: Description section: 'Calls from flight include a soft cheet or wheat, with perched birds giving a more drawn-out version.' It fills the shared program's alarm slot because the source describes no separate alarm call; loudness and cooldown are judgement.
